# Maximum probability reference vectors

`cara_frisbee.csv` contains 58 numeric test vectors derived from NASA CARA
Analysis Tools, <https://github.com/nasa/CARA_Analysis_Tools>, distributed
under the NASA Open Source Agreement (NOSA). Copyright (c) 2019–2025 United
States Government as represented by the Administrator of the National
Aeronautics and Space Administration. All Rights Reserved.

Each row records its source test file/line and source CDM state/covariance
lines. The expected probabilities and original acceptance tolerances come
from `DistributedMatlab/Maximum2DPc/UnitTests/FrisbeeMaxPc_UnitTest.m`:
tests 12–13 (lines 641–757) provide circle results at absolute tolerance
5e-7, justified there by rounding to 1e-6 in Frisbee's publication;
tests 14–27 (lines 759–1623) provide equal-area-square results at relative
tolerance 1e-2, matching the upstream validated-data tolerance. The two
circle cases additionally compare with the known populated-secondary
covariance integral to the upstream relative tolerance 1e-4.

The numeric projection is independently calculated in Python from CDM RTN
covariances, rotating each object's covariance into EME2000 and then the
relative encounter plane. Position and HBR columns are km; covariance
columns are km²; probabilities and tolerance values are dimensionless.
`epoch_utc` preserves the source TCA (including day-of-year date notation).
The circle reference uses SciPy QUADPACK and the square reference uses
normal CDF products after principal-axis rotation. Neither expected
probabilities nor reference probabilities are generated by the C++ module.

The algorithm references are `FrisbeeMaxPc.m` lines 94–179 (encounter
projection, Ka and rank-one unknown covariance) and `PcCircle.m` lines
475–495 (equal-area or circumscribed squares in principal axes). CARA's
finite-HBR Frisbee prescription does not mathematically maximize the disk
integral over all possible unknown covariances; the method name and header
document that distinction.

`pc_scaled_maximum_reference.csv` contains eight independent synthetic
closed-form Gaussian geometry inputs: 1 km miss, 0.01 km HBR, major-axis
sigma 1 km, sigma aspect ratios 3, 10, 100 and 1000, in an abstract fixed
encounter plane at an arbitrary common epoch. Rotated variants apply a
0.731-radian rigid rotation to both miss and covariance. SciPy QUADPACK
integrates the Gaussian disk probability and bounded scalar optimization
finds the maximum over a positive covariance scale. Native tests use 1e-7
relative probability tolerance to allow floating-point covariance rotation
at aspect 1000, and compare with a 1601-point logarithmic brute-force scale
scan (1e-6 relative bound allowance for quadrature/optimization roundoff).

Regenerate both files offline from the worktree root:

```sh
.oracle/venv/bin/python analysis/conjunction-assessment/scripts/regen-cara-frisbee-fixtures.py
```

No MATLAB source, `.mat` file, CDM file, or PDF is vendored here.
